answer: Seeded random-walk trust resists sybils: trust is a pulse released from a small set of known-honest seed nodes and spread by short random walks across the attestation graph; standing is how much of that walk lands on an identity. Sybils sit behind a thin boundary of attack edges, so the walk seldom crosses into their region — the ocean of honest nodes absorbs nearly all the probability mass. A farm can forge dense internal links, but that density cannot pull more walk-probability across the sparse cut dividing it from the seeds, so a thousand fakes share one vanishing trickle of landed trust.
